title: Best Corded and Specialist Vacuum Cleaners UK
short: Six corded, wet-and-dry, handheld and compact vacuums tested by Expert Reviews, for jobs a cordless stick doesn't cover.
intro: Not every cleaning job suits a cordless stick vacuum. This guide covers the corded, wet-and-dry and specialist machines from Expert Reviews' tested roundup of over 90 vacuums (for cordless stick vacuums, see our separate cordless vacuums guide). Vacuums are tested in a domestic setting on everyday tasks, plus measured spill tests using flour, Cheerios and pet hair on short-pile carpet and hard floor, weighing how much of each spill ends up in the bin after a single pass, along with suction and battery tests where relevant.

products.name: Henry Hoover HVR160
products.best_for: Anyone who wants a British institution with a huge bin and cheap running costs
products.key_spec: 620W, 9L bin, cylinder, 26.8m mains cable, optional bagless
products.summary: Expert Reviews found effective dust-gathering matched with pleasingly quiet performance, and a huge 9L bin capacity that dwarfs other vacuums in its roundup. The most recent model halved the power rating from 1,200W to 620W, but suction is still respectable. Its biggest appeal is value: replacement bags and filters are relatively cheap. The long cable can become tangled, it's best suited to smaller particles on carpet, and the basic floor head has no roller for deeper dirt.
cons: Best suited to smaller particles on carpet
Basic floor head has no roller for deeper dirt

products.name: Classic Upright Vacuum NV602UK
products.best_for: Carpet-focused homes on a budget who still want a lift-away hose
products.key_spec: 750W, 1.1L bin, corded upright, lift-away vacuuming unit and hose
products.summary: Expert Reviews found powerful suction and a lift-away unit and hose that helps it clean areas a traditional upright can't reach, at an affordable price for Shark's upright range. It only has a brush bar rather than Shark's dual floor head with a fluffy roller, so it isn't quite as effective on hard flooring, and it lacks Shark's anti-tangle technology, so the brush bar needs regular cleaning of long hair.
pros: Lift-away unit and hose reach awkward areas
cons: Only a brush bar, less effective on hard floor

products.name: George
products.best_for: Anyone who wants to vacuum and shampoo carpets and upholstery with one machine
products.key_spec: 15L bin, corded cylinder, wet and dry, washes carpets, hard floors and upholstery
products.summary: Expert Reviews found few vacuums perform as many functions as George: it vacuums like its red sibling Henry, but with adjustments can also wash carpets, hard floors and upholstery with water and detergent, sucking up the dirty water afterwards to leave the area almost dry. Its vacuuming relies solely on suction with no motorised roller brush, so it isn't the best clean on its own, but Expert Reviews calls it reasonable for the price.
pros: Vacuums, washes and dries carpets, hard floors and upholstery
Reasonable for the price given its versatility
cons: Vacuuming isn't the best clean, lacks a motorised roller
Not the best choice for hard floor vacuuming alone

products.name: ONEPWR Blade 5 Dual Pet & Car
products.badge: Best for hard floors, cars and pets
products.best_for: Mixed carpet and hard floor homes with pets or cars to clean
products.key_spec: Cordless, 3.9kg, dual-action floor head, two batteries included
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a dual-action floor head with a brush roller for carpet and a fluffy roller for hard floor that handles the transition between surfaces well, with the fluffy roller really helping it excel on hard floor. It didn't handle carpet quite as well as the best dual-roller Shark rivals, but performed well for the price. It comes with a generous set of pet and car accessories and two batteries, so one can charge while the other's in use.
pros: Handles carpet and hard floor cleaning well
Generous selection of pet and car accessories
cons: Doesn't handle carpet quite as well as the best dual-roller rivals
products.search: Vax ONEPWR Blade 5 Dual Pet Car

products.name: V12 Detect Slim
products.best_for: Smaller houses and flats that want Dyson power in a lighter, more compact vacuum
products.key_spec: Cordless, laser dust detection, brush roller and fluffy roller heads, live particle count display
products.summary: Expert Reviews found all the tools and features of a flagship Dyson cordless stick in a smaller, lighter, more convenient format. It has separate floor heads for carpet and hard floor, with the fluffy roller's green laser illuminating dirt and dust, and a screen that displays live particle counts and doubles as a control panel and battery indicator.
pros: Full Dyson cleaning power in a smaller, lighter format
Laser dust detection on the hard floor head

products.name: WandVac 2.0
products.best_for: Quick clean-ups on sofas, car seats and upholstery that don't need a full vacuum
products.key_spec: 0.6kg, 100ml bin, 15-minute battery, charging station, boost button
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a small, light wand vacuum that sits on its charging station, always ready for quick jobs. It comes with a dusting brush and crevice tool plus an upholstery nozzle for furniture and car seats, and a boost button increases suction when needed. It managed spills well in testing, though the tiny bin needs emptying after each significant use.
pros: Small, light and always charged on its station
Comes with dusting, crevice and upholstery attachments
cons: Tiny bin needs emptying after each significant use

guide.a: Cylinder vacuums like the Henry Hoover and Numatic George typically have larger bin capacity but you drag them behind you. Uprights like the Shark Classic take up less space for storage and are less cumbersome to manoeuvre, though they usually need emptying more often.

Bagged vacuums like the Henry Hoover keep dust neatly contained and are tidy to empty, at the cost of buying replacement bags. Bagless models store dirt in a see-through bin, which can be messy to empty but saves on running costs.

guide.q: Is a wet-and-dry vacuum worth it?
guide.a: If you want to shampoo carpets and upholstery as well as vacuum, the Numatic George does both, sucking up dirty water to leave surfaces almost dry. Its vacuuming alone isn't as thorough as a dedicated vacuum with a motorised brush roll, so it suits mixed jobs rather than being your only vacuum.

guide.q: Do I need a separate handheld vacuum?
guide.a: A dedicated handheld like the Shark WandVac 2.0 is worth it if you often vacuum sofas, car seats or small spills and don't want to get a full-size vacuum out. Its short battery life and small bin suit quick jobs rather than a full clean.
